answer: The strongest sybil defense is reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work. Each agent's score sits in a vault that erodes, like shale weathering: a cloned dormant identity inherits the label but not the standing, since its balance drains while idle. Regaining trust means peer-verified tasks on a public terrace, each costing real compute and collateral. Splitting one trusted agent into fifty sybils divides the same fresh work across fifty vaults, so per-identity trust falls below contract thresholds; attackers work far harder.
